text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Crown Prince Sidi Mohammed in an Eid al-Adha message to King Hassan reaffirms constant mobilisation to defend Moslem sacred values.
- Prine Moulay Rachid inaugurates olympic swimming pool in Rabat.
- Morocco exported 2,400 tonnes of orange to Saudi Arabia and United Arab Emirates in the 1996-1997 season.
- Former U.S. Secretary of State James Baker, the U.N. secretary-general's personal envoy for the Western Sahara, starts visit to Morocco and Algeria on April 22.
- Experts in Morocco's forecasting Centre Marocain de Conjoncture say first estimates put Morocco's Gross Domestic Product growth rate at minus one percent in the first quarter of 1997.
- A Moroccan expatriate jumps to his death to escape fire in his home in four-storey building in Brussels.
- King Hassan presides over Eid al-Adha prayer and receives congratulations from senior officials.
- James Baker starts an "emergency mission" in the North African region. Moroccan Sahraouis display their attachment to their homeland and the Alaouite Throne.
